stops.note: timber and building stuff; Vitruvius's De architectura (c. 20s BC) gives advice on felling and choosing it
'wood': João Gonçalves Zarco and Tristão Vaz Teixeira reached the island around 1419-20 and named it for its dense forest
the island's fortified wine; in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1 (c. 1597) Poins teases Falstaff for selling his soul 'for a cup of Madeira and a cold capon's leg'

current_meaning: a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of Madeira
